clue.text: The royal house set trap — about time!

indicators.note: the two outer pieces sit about, that is around, the word for time

parts.note: to plant something is to set it in place
a net is a trap for fish or birds
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A royal dynasty lays a snare and someone exclaims that it is high time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set trap' reads as one phrase but splits into two separate pieces; 'about' then wraps them around the word for time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenets were the dynasty that ruled England from Henry II to Richard III.

clue.text: Soothe the head about state set-up

annotationWithheld.why: Soothe the head about state set-up: PATE around LA (state) and CA, but 'about' must be both CA and the container signal; no parse without a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Soothe the head about state set-up

clue.text: Spy for a guy

parts.note: a gent is a man or chap

explanation.surface: A spy is sought to stand in for some fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret agent is a spy working for an intelligence service.

clue.text: Forming designs on the clients

parts.note: reads like scheming against customers, but literally describes a parlour artist inking pictures onto customers' skin

explanation.surface: Someone is plotting to exploit their customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Inking pictures into a customer's skin is the craft of the body-art parlour.

clue.text: In spring rewards will be increased

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words spring rewards, run across the word break

explanation.surface: A promise that springtime bonuses will rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow is to get bigger, so a thing that has risen in size has grown.

clue.text: Little bird sanctuary on the heath

parts.note: a nest is a snug refuge or retreat
ling is the heather of moorland and heath

explanation.surface: A bird reserve set out on open moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: LING is the common heather that covers British heaths; 'on' places one piece after the other in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird still too small to leave its home is a nestling.

clue.text: Covers for heels

explanation.surface: Something to protect the heels of shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilt is an old word for a canvas awning or cover, and a ship that heels over leans or tilts.

clue.text: Woman having two articles put into safe-keeping

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
the indefinite article is a
the definite article is the

explanation.surface: A woman with a couple of possessions places them somewhere secure.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a sword is to slip it into its scabbard for protection.

clue.text: A boy in a rush used his head

indicators.note: the boy goes in the plant, splitting it

parts.note: a reed or rush is a tall waterside plant
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad in a hurry still thought things through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rush' looks like haste but is the waterside plant; 'in' signals that the boy goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reasoned used logic, thinking a matter through with the brain.

clue.text: A number enter new craft, showing watchfulness

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of enter are made into something fresh

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a sea craft

explanation.surface: Several people board a new boat and stay on the lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert means staying watchful and attentive.

clue.text: Superior European university

explanation.surface: A top-ranking seat of learning on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal lord, one's superior, is a liege; Liège in Belgium has a well-known university.

clue.text: Fighting unit in a London suburb

indicators.note: the one goes in the suburb's name

parts.note: Acton is a district of west London
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

explanation.surface: A military detachment is stationed out in the London suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a suburb in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who see action are engaged in combat.

clue.text: Points into the cupboard, being dense

indicators.note: the points are put into the cupboard

parts.note: a closet is a cupboard
S and E are two compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Someone directs things into a cupboard, a little slow on the uptake.
explanation.definitionFit: Things packed tightly together are thick and dense, like close-set trees.

clue.text: One finds this really sickening

parts.note: sounds like disgust at something, but literally names a substance that makes the taker vomit

explanation.surface: A person declares something truly revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that induces vomiting is literally sickening.

clue.text: Trapped Oriental bad-men put out

parts.note: E for east, the Orient

indicators.note: bad indicates the letters of men go wrong

parts.note: to shed is to put out or cast off

explanation.surface: An Eastern villain has been ensnared and evicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad-men' looks like villains, but 'bad' is the anagram signal working on MEN, giving NME.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught in a mesh or net means snared.

clue.text: An example of the popular attitude

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a stance is a position or attitude

explanation.surface: A case study of public opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case illustrating something.

clue.text: Perhaps a car to enthral one?

explanation.surface: A motor might captivate its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is one form of conveyance for people, and to send someone into raptures is to carry them away.

clue.text: Left content in new squeeze…

indicators.note: the left letter is the content held in the word for new

parts.note: something new and unfamiliar is strange

explanation.surface: A leftover contents squeeze in a new container.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle someone is to squeeze their throat.

clue.text: Sheepish creatures get a break by the sea

parts.note: rams are male sheep

indicators.note: break signals the letters of get a are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Sheep escape through a gap in a fence on the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' turns GET A into GATE. Ramsgate is a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsgate is a resort town on the Kent coast, so it lies beside the water.

clue.text: … following strike-left in sympathy

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: After a hit, someone is left feeling compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is close understanding and fellow feeling between people.

clue.text: Colour when getting angrier

explanation.surface: Someone goes red in the face as their temper rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Madder is a plant yielding a red dye, and someone growing more furious is crosser.

clue.text: Taking note, goes for interest

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
turns means goes, as in goes sour

explanation.surface: Someone takes notes and goes along out of curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns are the profit or yield earned on an investment.

clue.text: Minister, a Labour leader of the country

parts.note: a pastor is a church minister

indicators.note: only the first letter of Labour, its leader, is used

explanation.surface: A government minister and a Labour Party chief of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes rural life and countryside scenes.

clue.text: Talk or eat without S restraint

indicators.note: the letters of or eat run wild, free of order, and rearrange
the letters of or eat run wild, free of order, and rearrange

explanation.surface: Advice to chatter or dine freely.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak at length in a formal way.

clue.text: Company bringing little cold store into use

indicators.note: the rearranged word brings the cold letter inside it
store is put to a new use, its letters reorganised

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
C is short for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A firm puts a small cold store into operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into use' turns STORE into ESORT; 'bringing' takes C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps another company or accompanies them acts as an escort.

clue.text: A barbeque, that would be best!

explanation.surface: A cookout would be the finest thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as OUT DO, an outdoor party such as a barbecue.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor party such as a barbecue is an out do, and to surpass someone is to beat them.

clue.text: Nail for railway poster

parts.note: BR is British Rail
an ad, or advertisement, is a poster

explanation.surface: Fixing a railway advertisement with a pin.
explanation.definitionFit: A brad is a thin flat nail with a small head.

clue.text: Greek character in some gainful occupation

indicators.note: the letters sit in some gainful, crossing the word gap

explanation.surface: A Greek person in a profitable job.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Putting rubbish in order, he's choked

indicators.note: the rubbish goes in the order

parts.note: the Garter is the senior order of English knighthood
rot is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone tidying junk gets overcome with emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is the Order of the Garter, not tidiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler who used a cord on his victims has done the throttling.

clue.text: Improvements made in stone building

indicators.note: building means the letters of made in stone are constructed into a new form

explanation.surface: Upgrades carried out on a stone building.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrections and revisions to a text improve it.
